experiment_design.technical_details: The experiment tests the hypothesis that self-evolving agents (e.g., EpiEvolve) detect regime shifts in streaming epidemiological data earlier than static models. The core mechanism relies on dynamic adaptation of internal representations during distributional shifts, contrasting with fixed-parameter Poisson regression and standard time-series models. The study uses retrospective simulation on historical outbreak data to measure 'time-to-detection' of exponential growth phases. Key technical components include: (1) A streaming data simulator injecting regime shifts into historical COVID-19 or similar outbreak trajectories; (2) Implementation of a self-evolving agent architecture capable of online learning; (3) Baseline implementations of Over-dispersed Poisson Regression and ARIMA/LSTM time-series models; (4) Statistical testing of detection latency differences.

3. Detection Logic: Define an 'alert' when model prediction error or internal state change exceeds a calibrated threshold. 
4. Evaluation: Calculate time difference between ground-truth shift and model alert.
